NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday took a dig at BJP supporters for flagging the misspelling of Union minister Nirmala Sitharaman 's name in a social media post by Rahul Gandhi , saying the deliberate typo was a strategy to draw attention.In a post on X, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate thanked BJP supporters for amplifying Rahul Gandhi's post in which he accused the government of “criminally destroying” the Tata Group ."BJP buffoons fall prey so easily. In communication, deliberate misspelling is a strategy to gain attention. It’s called Typo Marketing," the Congress leader said."Thank you for amplifying Rahul ji’s tweet on Tata by desperately pointing out Sitaraman misspelt. Hahhahaha!" she added.Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul and Sitharaman sparred on X after the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha accused the government of “criminally destroying” the Tata Group amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the conglomerate. Rahul alleged that no business leader dared to speak out against the alleged interference.In a post on X, the Congress leader said, "Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word.How long will you stay silent? Until they own you?" He added that Indian businesses were not Prime Minister Narendra Modi's and home minister Amit Shah's "plaything" and accused business leaders of lacking the courage to speak out.Sitharaman hit back at Rahul, accusing him of trying to incite business leaders to join him in spreading "distrust and toxicity". She urged him to refrain from politicising every issue and said casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal was unacceptable.Defending the government's policies, Sitharaman said the Modi government valued Indian industry as a source of jobs and economic growth. She also accused the Congress of having stifled Indian entrepreneurs for decades through the "Licence-Quota Raj" and said the government's policies were designed to support enterprise, industry and investment.Responding with another X post, Rahul wrote, "Dear Mrs. Sitarama (sic), 1. Earlier this week, Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata challenged the September 17 board resolution of Tata Sons to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as chairman of the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate.
Article Summary: Congress takes a dig at BJP supporters for flagging the misspelling of Union minister Nirmala Sitharaman's name in a social media post by Rahul Gandhi. In a post on X, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate thanked BJP supporters. Rahul accused the government of “criminally destroying” the Tata Group amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the conglomerate.

Article Title: Thousands of years of knowledge, struggle shaped India as cultural nation: Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
Article Text:
Sekhawat was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Wednesday said India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, struggle and experience.Shekhawat was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi' at the Dharohar Bhawan, the headquarters of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), which hosted the event along with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA).The book has been published by IGNCA and Subhi Publications and edited by former Rajya Sabha member Tarun Vijay."India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries, but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, spiritual practice, struggle and experience. India's civilisation and cultural consciousness have flowed uninterrupted through centuries," Shekhawat said."India has established connections with civilisations across the world through dialogue and cultural exchange.Its knowledge traditions, architectural heritage and cultural legacy have attracted many countries around the world," he added.During the colonial rule, "efforts were made to weaken Indians' sense of pride" in their civilisation, culture and traditions. This also influenced the way Indians viewed their own knowledge traditions and cultural ideals, an IGNCA statement quoted the minister as saying."The distinctive feature of Indian civilisation is its ability to draw inspiration from the past while moving towards the future. Ideals represented by Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, along with the traditions of sages, thinkers and seekers of knowledge, remain important foundations for India's cultural consciousness," he said.The book explores the role of monuments in preserving and revitalising India's cultural identity, alongside the discourse surrounding the nation's historical memory.It gives particular importance to monument preservation and the idea of "decolonising the nation's memory", highlighting the need to understand India's cultural heritage through its "own historical experiences, traditions and cultural outlook", the statement said.Union Minister of State Jitendra Singh, former Rajya Sabha member and ex-president of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, were present on the occasion, among others.In a separate statement, the tourism ministry said the Indian Culinary Institute (ICI) on Wednesday signed an MoU with the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), providing for the recognition of ICI's BBA and MBA programmes by the JNU, enabling the university to award degrees to students completing these courses at ICI.The MoU was signed by JNU V-C Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit and Gyan Bhushan, Director, ICI, in the presence of Shekhawat and Tourism Secretary Bhuvnesh Kumar.The recognition of ICI's BBA and MBA programmes by JNU, commencing from the next academic year, is expected to enhance academic and professional opportunities for the students, the statement said.
Article Summary: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said India is a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, struggle and experience. He was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi'

Article Title: Cyclone Arnab: Amit Shah speaks to four CMs, says relief operations on 'war footing'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday took stock of the impact of cyclone Arnab and spoke to the chief ministers of Andhra Pradesh , Puducherry, Odisha and Chhattisgarh; adding that centre will give all assistance and relief operations are on "War footing"."In the wake of Cyclone Arnab, spoke with the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, Odisha and Chhattisgarh and assured them of every assistance to mitigate the hardship of the people in the face of the disaster," he said in a post on X.Further giving info on rescue and relief, he added, " NDRF and SDRF teams have sprung into action and are continuing rescue and relief operations on a war footing. Article Title: ‘Unwavering commitment’: Rajnath Singh backs ASEAN centrality, calls for stronger defence ties

Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday reaffirmed India’s commitment to ASEAN centrality and called for stronger defence cooperation and mutual trust at the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines.“India reiterates its unwavering commitment to ASEAN centrality, which is a cornerstone of our Act East Policy and Indo-Pacific vision,” Singh said, expressing gratitude to the Philippines for hosting the meeting and extending warm hospitality.He said the forum was important for maintaining a resilient, secure and prosperous region, adding that the discussions should help address emerging disruptions and strengthen cooperation among participating countries.“I look forward to constructive deliberations and concrete outcomes from this meeting,” Singh said.Philippine defence secretary Gilberto C Teodoro Jr, meanwhile, said two documents were signed at the ADMM the previous day — a joint statement commemorating the 50th anniversary commitment to shared principles, ASEAN unity and centrality.He outlined three priorities for the meeting: ensuring cooperation is guided by mutual respect and international law, sustaining progress under the ADMM-Plus framework, and addressing the wider impact of global disruptions.Highlighting the importance of food and energy security amid supply chain challenges and overseas conflicts, Teodoro also called for greater cooperation to protect migrant workers and seafarers, particularly those from smaller countries caught in conflict zones.He said the international order had a special obligation to protect migrant workers and seafarers, recognising their contribution to the global economy and the countries in which they work.“Together, let us create a safer and more prosperous Article Title: Supreme Court removes October 30 deadline for additions to Delhi electoral roll
Article Text:
Supreme Court asked the Election Commission not to stop adding names to Delhi's electoral rolls by the October 30 deadline

How can you insist on Form 6 for person who was voter earlier: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a relief to over 43 lakh voters excluded from Delhi’s draft electoral rolls for ‘permanently shifting out’, Supreme Court on Wednesday asked Election Commission not to stop adding names in the voter list by the Oct 30 deadline and told it to continue distributing and receiving enumeration forms, and Forms 6 (new voters), 7 (for deletion) and 8 (for those who shifted from one constituency to another).A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also questioned EC on why voters whose names were there on earlier electoral rolls but were deleted from the draft rolls were asked to file Form 6, which is meant for enrolment of first-time voters.Without passing any order, the bench said, “We will examine the issue after two weeks. The effort should be to reduce the 43 lakh (who have been deleted from draft rolls). One suggestion — publish the list of those who are deleted and specify the reason for deletion against each name. Request them to contact the nearest BLO and fill Form 8. You can give them enumeration forms. Tell them that they are welcome to fill either Form 6 or 8. ”During the proceedings on a PIL filed by activist Anjali Bhardwaj, the bench heard advocate Prashant Bhushan’s complaints against EC for insisting on filling Form 6 by those whose names got excluded and, thereby, compelling them to give a false declaration that they were first-time voters.The bench said, “Right to vote is a vital right. If a person has shifted out from Vasant Kunj to Dwarka, or had gone out of station for a month or so and for some other reason could not respond to the EC notice or could not file the claim for inclusion of name, or did not get enumeration form because of change of address, should EC permanently disable him from voting by striking his name off the voter list?“How can you insist on Form 6 for a person who was a voter earlier? If a person has shifted from one constituency to another within Delhi, it is erroneous to ask him/her to fill Form 6. You must allow similarly placed persons, whose names are deleted on the ground of ‘permanently shifted’, to fill Form 8.”Appearing for EC, senior advocate D S Naidu said the commission had conducted over one lakh camps in Delhi to spread awareness among people on how to re-enter their names in the voter list.“The situation on the ground is very different. Not a single person has come to fill Form 8. The petitioner is creating a scare on paper in the courtroom. Any person can seek inclusion of his/her name in the voter list of a constituency till the date of filing of nominations,” Naidu said, and clarified that no one has been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore names in voter lists across states.But EC relented to keep the window open for inclusion of names in Delhi as SC insisted that the Oct 30 deadline for filing claims and objections need not be set in stone as elections were not imminent in Delhi to warrant urgent completion of the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asked the Election Commission not to stop adding names to Delhi's electoral rolls by the October 30 deadline. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also questioned EC on why voters whose names were there on earlier electoral rolls but were deleted from draft rolls were asked to file Form 6.

Article Title: Delhi HC rejects PIL against passport fee hike for NRIs
Article Text:
File photo: Indian passport

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Wednesday dismissed a PIL challenging the central govt’s decision to increase passport fees for non-resident Indians (NRIs), observing that a 67% hike after a gap of 14 years is not “unreasonable or exorbitant”. Acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma added that the decision to determine the fees falls within the policy domain of the govt and judicial intervention was not warranted.Pravasi Legal Cell filed the petition, alleging discrimination against NRIs, who are required to pay around Rs 11,900 for passports, compared to Rs 2,500 for resident Indians.
Article Summary: Delhi high court dismissed a PIL challenging the central govt’s decision to increase passport fees for non-resident Indians. Acting chief justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and justice Sanjay Sharma added that the decision to determine the fees falls within the policy domain of the govt.

Article Title: Privacy law doesn’t infringe upon press freedom: IT & I&B minister
Article Text:
File photo: Union minister for railways, information & broadcasting, and electronics & IT Ashwini Vaishnaw

NEW DELHI: IT & I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Wednesday said the Digital Personal Data Protection Act does not infringe upon press freedom, amid concerns from news publishers that the law could hinder investigative reporting. He said the Constitution’s guarantee of press freedom remains paramount and secure.TOI has learnt that govt would be open to amending the law to explicitly safeguard journalistic work and would also invite editors and other media professionals to have a detailed discussion on their concerns.“Journalistic freedom is guaranteed by the Constitution of India. That freedom is absolutely available. There is not even an intention to affect journalistic freedom,” Vaishnaw told mediapersons. He was responding to questions over the issue in light of a legal challenge by news publishers to the new law’s potential implications for reporting on matters of public interest.Vaishnaw said the enactment of the new Act had followed a Supreme Court judgement recognising the right to privacy as a fundamental right and was framed after more than a year of consultations involving newspapers, television channels, media representatives, IT industry and other stakeholders.He added that during the consultation process, govt had explained that the legislation would not undermine press freedom.“It was clearly explained that provisions of the DPDP Act nowhere infringe upon freedom of the press, journalism and freedom of media,” the minister said. He argued that the constitutional guarantee of press freedom could not be overridden by data-protection legislation, distinguishing the misuse of private information from its legitimate use in journalism.Vaishnaw also said that he would invite all editors and mediapersons to have an open dialogue with govt. “We will be very happy to explain, and if there is any doubt, we will be happy to take on record any suggestion and act if there is a need to.”
Article Summary: IT & I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the Digital Personal Data Protection Act does not infringe upon press freedom. He was responding to questions over the issue in light of a legal challenge by news publishers to the new law’s potential implications.

Article Title: 'We don't want a fight': Delhi traders' body writes to Rahul Gandhi again over November 1 rally
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A Delhi traders' body on Wednesday wrote another letter to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , urging him to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Diwali over fears that the gathering could disrupt business in several major markets.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI), which has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales, also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred.In the letter, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted an opportunity to put forward their concerns about the rally, which is expected to draw around 10 lakh people."We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders. So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy," Goyal said.The traders' body also proposed that it would withdraw its protest if Gandhi could convince its representatives that the rally would bring more customers and boost business. However, if traders were able to convince him that the event would result in losses, they wanted him to agree to postpone it until after Diwali.Wednesday's letter was the second sent by CTI to Gandhi within four days. The organisation had first approached the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha on October 24, seeking postponement of the rally to prevent disruptions during one of the busiest periods for Delhi's markets.According to CTI, at least 20 markets within a 1-5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan could be affected by the expected turnout.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj.Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market are also among the commercial areas identified by the traders' body.The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori" and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The opposition alliance has called the November 1 rally to step up pressure on the government and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The rally follows a series of demonstrations by opposition parties over the electoral-roll revision exercise.On October 12, opposition leaders, including Gandhi, joined activists and civil society members in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route near the Supreme Court in Delhi. A joint petition challenging the SIR was also filed.A day later, Gandhi hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his residence. Following the meeting, the opposition alliance vowed to continue its campaign and take the fight to its logical conclusion.
Article Summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales. It also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred. The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori"

NEW DELHI: The Australian government on Monday expanded biometric collection requirements for visa applicants in India from October 26, introducing fingerprint and facial image collection for certain new visa applications.The change covers applications filed on or after that date, while those submitted earlier and visas already issued remain unaffected, the Australian high commission said. The department of home affairs will inform applicants who need to complete the additional step and explain how to do so.Applicants may be directed to one of 16 biometric collection centres operated by VFS Global across India. Those who meet the eligibility criteria may instead be able to submit their biometrics through the Australian Immi App.The government said the move is intended to make identity checks more reliable, curb fraud and protect applicants from identity misuse. Australia already collects biometric data from visa applicants in nearly 60 countries, and the extension brings India into the programme.Visa processing times are not expected to be adversely affected if applicants provide their biometrics promptly after being notified.Applicants have been advised not to book an appointment or use the app until they receive an official notification from the department of home affairs.The Australian government said applicants’ personal information would be handled under relevant laws and transferred through encrypted channels.It also clarified that buying optional services from service providers would not affect either processing times or visa decisions.
Article Summary: Australia introduces fingerprint and facial image requirements for certain new visa applications from India, effective Oct 26. The government said the move is intended to make identity checks more reliable, curb fraud and protect applicants from identity misuse. The change covers applications filed on or after that date, while those submitted earlier and visas already issued remain unaffected.

GURGAON: The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application by US-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development for BPaL, a life-saving tuberculosis therapy, citing lack of novelty and inventive step. The decision could allow domestic drugmakers to launch cheaper generic versions in India and other high-burden countries, health experts said.Govt provides BPaL, a combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, free under National TB Elimination Programme. However, treatment costs remain a challenge. The six-month all-oral regimen is shorter than older treatments and reduces patients’ compliance burden. More than 15,000 patients have begun BPaLM, which adds moxifloxacin, under the programme.Pre-grant oppositions were filed separately by Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust’s Eldred Tellis and TB survivor Ganesh Acharya, supported by Lawyers’ Collective and Médécins Sans Frontières Access Campaign; and Delhi Network of Positive People, supported by Third World Network.Patent Controller upheld grounds of lack of novelty, lack of inventive step, non-patentability and insufficient disclosure, refusing application under Sec 15 of Patents Act.Opponents argued the combination and its use in a shorter regimen had been disclosed in scientific research dating to 2015.The opposition invoked Sections 3(d), 3(e) and 3(i), which restrict patents on new uses of known substances, exclude mere admixtures and methods of medical treatment. All four grounds were upheld.TB Alliance had earlier licensed generic firms, including Macleods Pharma and Lupin, to manufacture pretomanid for BPaL in India, though health activists called the agreements restrictive. This could widen the supplier pool.
Article Summary: Patent application by US-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development for BPaL rejected. Decision could allow domestic drugmakers to launch cheaper generic versions in India and other high-burden countries. Govt provides BPaLM, a combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, free under National TB Elimination Programme.

Article Title: Isro to launch NVS-03 on Oct 30, but NavIC has a long way to go
Article Text:
NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series

Why the launch matters

A troubled programme

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Still a long road

BENGALURU: Isro will launch its next navigation satellite, NVS-03, aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket on Friday (Oct 30) at 11.51 pm from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.GSLV-F18 is the 20th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). The mission is a crucial attempt to rebuild India’s ailing NavIC navigation constellation, which currently lacks enough operational satellites to provide standalone positioning services.The roughly 50-metre rocket, with a lift-off mass of about 420 tonnes, will place the approximately 2,250-kg NVS-03 into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a perigee (closest point to Earth) of 170 km, apogee (farthest point from Earth) of 37,023 km and inclination of 20.75°.NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series, designed to ensure continuity of the services of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, now called Navigation with Indian Constellation, or NavIC.NavIC is intended to provide Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services across India and up to about 1,500 km beyond the country’s landmass, reducing dependence on foreign navigation systems.“NVS-03 carries an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured clocks and introduces the L1 signal, in addition to the existing L5 and S signals,” Isro said. The addition is expected to widen compatibility with more user devices and strengthen NavIC’s civilian and strategic utility.But the launch comes at a time when NavIC is operating below its minimum requirement. Earlier this year, union minister Jitendra Singh told Parliament: “After completion of mission life (10 years) of IRNSS-1F, presently the NavIC constellation has three satellites — IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 — for providing PNT services.To provide basic positioning service, a minimum of four operational satellites are required in orbit.” The govt acknowledged that, as a result, “the NavIC constellation cannot provide standalone positioning service, however timing service is functional.”NavIC’s difficulties stem from a combination of ageing satellites, atomic-clock failures and a failed replenishment mission. IRNSS-1F completed its 10-year mission life in March 2026; soon after, Isro said its procured onboard atomic clock stopped functioning, removing the satellite from navigation service.The more immediate setback was NVS-02, launched on Jan 29, 2025 aboard GSLV-F15. Although the satellite separated successfully and deployed its solar panels, it could not perform the orbit-raising manoeuvres needed to move from its elliptical transfer orbit to its designated circular orbit.An Isro apex committee traced the anomaly to the spacecraft’s pyro system. It found that the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve in the oxidiser line of the orbit-raising engine, preventing the engine from firing. The committee concluded that the most likely cause was disengagement of at least one contact in each of the main and redundant connector paths.Isro said the panel recommended corrective measures to enhance redundancy and improve the reliability of pyro-system operations, and that these recommendations have already been implemented.NVS-03’s successful launch would raise the number of navigation-capable satellites, but it will not by itself restore NavIC to full operational strength. The spacecraft must first complete orbit-raising manoeuvres, reach its designated orbit and be validated for service.The govt has said NVS-04 and NVS-05 are in an advanced stage of realisation, meaning further launches will be needed before NavIC regains a robust, redundant constellation.NavIC’s return to standalone positioning service depends not only on NVS-03 reaching orbit, but on Isro executing the post-launch operations that failed for NVS-02, and on the timely induction of the satellites that follow.
Article Summary: NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series. It is designed to ensure continuity of the services of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System. NavIC is intended to provide Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services across India.

Article Title: IN-SPACe picks 6 AI space projects for grants of up to Rs 1-cr each
Article Text:
Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre

BENGALURU: Space regulator-cum-promoter Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected six private space-sector entities for seed-fund grants under its AI INSPIRED programme, which aims to encourage the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in space technology.The projects span precision landing, space situational awareness, debris detection, satellite servicing and refuelling, automated target recognition, and spacecraft autonomy. Two other entities have been selected for mentorship and technical support, including access to Isro facilities for technology validation.The programme, announced in Feb 2026 under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme, has a total outlay of up to Rs 6 crore, with each selected entity eligible for a grant of up to Rs 1 crore. The funding is intended to help start-ups and micro and small enterprises develop AI-based solutions for space applications.Among the selected projects, Agnikul Cosmos will develop an edge AI-enabled vision-based terminal navigation module for precision landing. The technology is aimed at improving navigation during the final stages of a landing manoeuvre.Digantara has been selected for its Agentic RSO Evaluation Suite (ARES), while EON Space Labs will develop an intelligent optical payload using field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based edge AI.The latter project aims to enable real-time space situational awareness and detection of space debris.OrbitAid Aerospace will work on machine-learning-assisted pose estimation algorithms for on-orbit servicing and refuelling. Such algorithms can help spacecraft determine their relative positions and orientations, an important requirement for operations involving approaching, docking with or servicing another spacecraft.Omnipresent Robot Technologies has been selected for an automated target recognition project covering applications such as defence and docking. TakeMeToSpace will work on adaptive spacecraft autonomy through an AI modernisation programme for attitude determination and control systems (ADCS), which help establish a spacecraft's orientation and maintain its intended direction.IN-SPACe has also selected Foucault Private Limited and AkashaVeda Technologies for mentorship and technical support, although they are not listed among the six seed-fund grantees.Foucault will work on an autonomous collision avoidance system for spacecraft using AI and machine learning. AkashaVeda’s project focuses on AI-based mission management, covering both onboard and ground operations. The two entities will receive opportunities to use IN-SPACe and Isro facilities to validate their technologies. They will also be considered for technology transfer from the Department of Space.As per IN-SPACe, the initiative is part of its efforts to expand private participation in India’s space sector by supporting the development of indigenous technologies and products.
Article Summary: The projects span precision landing, space situational awareness, debris detection, satellite servicing and refuelling, automated target recognition, and spacecraft autonomy. The funding is intended to help start-ups and micro and small enterprises develop AI-based solutions for space applications.

New Delhi: Govt is targeting to mobilise $220 billion in investment in the renewable energy sector by 2030 to expand manufacturing, transmission infrastructure and green hydrogen production, as it prepares to host the four-day Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) in the capital from Nov 2 to 5.While solar energy projects would require an investment of nearly $70 billion, wind projects would need $25-30 billion, energy storage deployment $20 billion, transmission networks $40-45 billion, hydropower $12-15 billion and green hydrogen offtake $20-25 billion. India aims to achieve 500 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.The summit will be inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi at Bharat Mandapam on Nov 2 and is likely to be attended by energy ministers from 30 countries, including Australia, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom, as well as representatives of the European Union, with the aim of exploring cooperation in renewable energy financing, green hydrogen, energy storage, clean energy manufacturing and technology development.Santosh Sarangi, secretary in Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), said India had secured $64 billion in private investment between June 2024, when the previous RE-Invest Summit was held, and June 2026, including $6.2 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI).“With 308 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, we are firmly on course to reach our 500 GW target by 2030. Realising this ambition will require approximately $220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030, alongside accelerated deployment of energy storage, stronger transmission networks and expanded domestic manufacturing capabilities,” Sarangi said, adding that financial investors, private equity firms, pension funds and mutual funds were expected to play a key role in it.Ministry is also developing a framework to assign exploration rights for geothermal energy, similar to the guidelines on petroleum exploration, which is expected to be ready within a month or two.BRESE 2026 will be held alongside the 9th Session of International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH).Sarangi said Indian green hydrogen developers have so far secured orders for about 5.5 lakh tonnes per annum (MTPA), including 4.5 lakh MTPA secured in 2026 alone. Japan, South Korea and the EU were looking at greater sourcing of green ammonia and green methanol.He said green hydrogen had huge potential, with several pilot projects already under way in the direct reduced iron (DRI) steel and transportation sectors. India is also conducting an experiment across 10,000 acres in six states, covering 10 different crops, to inject ammonia directly into the soil instead of applying urea, a move that could improve efficiency and reduce costs and losses due to volatilisation and irrigation, Sarangi said.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar to be prime venue for India Biennale
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar (File Photo)

Biennale: Red Fort also among venues

Cultural engagement and community involvement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Within days of denotifying the area around Jantar Mantar as a protest site, the Centre has quickly moved in to select the 18th-century protected monument as one of the prime venues that will showcase exhibitions and programmes curated across over a dozen monuments and other prominent locations at “India Biennale 2026” that starts on Dec 4 and will be on till March 21.The first India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale was held at Red Fort in 2023 but its scale was limited. India Biennale 2026 is being called the second edition, but has been conceptualised by the culture ministry as a first of its kind in terms of scale and the ambition to bring together the best of art, architecture and design from across India and over 20 other countries.Nine countries, including France, Italy, Hungary, Switzerland and Sri Lanka, have already confirmed participation in ‘India Biennale 2026’.The list of monuments that will be venues for exhibitions, performances and experiences includes Purana Qila, Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Hauz Khas, Agrasen Ki Baoli, Humayun’s Tomb, Lodhi Garden, Mehrauli, Qila Rai Pithora, Safdarjung Tomb, Sabz Burj, Firozshah Kotla, Sakri Ghumti, Choti Ghumti. These are listed for now on the website and it is learnt that Jantar Mantar too will be added to the list soon.The list of venues also includes National Museum, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, National Gallery of Modern Art, Lalit Kala Akademi and Sangeet Natak Akademi.Sources said that the decision to use Jantar Mantar as a venue was taken after the area surrounding it was notified as a “no protest” zone in the wake of protests for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.For over three decades, the astronomical observatory was the designated protest site, but its proximity to Parliament and important govt offices had long been cited as a concern. India Biennale may be among the first major events to be hosted at the venue, which is in the heart of the city with metro stations close by.The website of the Biennale introduces the vision in grand terms. “For 108 days, Delhi monuments become the canvas”. “From Dec 4 to March 21, Delhi’s heritage monuments, museums, galleries, public spaces and communities come together under a single curatorial vision,” it declares.

Article Title: OCI cardholder can’t spread word of god sans govt nod: Madras HC
Article Text:
Madras high court





CHENNAI: Preachings and activities to spread the word of ‘God’, by an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) would fall within the meaning of missionary activity requiring special permission, Madras high court has said.Justice Bharatha Chakravarthy made the observation on Wednesday while confirming an order dated Sept 4, passed by the Bureau of Immigration cancelling the OCI permit granted to John Daniel, a US citizen.According to the petitioner, he visits India to meet his family members, pays respects to his elders at their graves in the Madras Cemeteries Board Trust Christian Cemetery, Kilpauk Garden Road, Chennai, visits his mother, and preserves close familial bonds. He claimed that he had not violated any law governing OCI cardholders and denied the allegations of missionary activities and religious conversions.Refusing to concur with the submissions, the court pointed out that substantial materials had been produced against the petitioner, indicating that he had consistently been addressing congregations, gatherings and meetings at various places in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh and that advertisements had been issued inviting the general public to attend his meetings.“Those materials cannot be regarded as fabricated or concocted,” the court said.“It is one thing to contend that the petitioner is not involved in conversion and is only spreading the message of ‘God’. However, it is not only for conversion, but even to be a missionary preaching his religion, it is only a prior permission that is mandated,” the court said.“The petitioner has made a categorical and sweeping statement before this court that he has never been involved in any missionary activities in India and has visited India only to see his mother, family and friends, which, on the face of it, is a lie,” the court said.“The petitioner will be free to apply for a regular visa to visit his mother. For conduct of his meetings and religious purposes, he can carry out his activities in India only upon being granted the requisite official permission,” the court added and dismissed the plea.
Article Summary: Madras high court says preachings and activities to spread the word of ‘God’ by an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) would fall within the meaning of missionary activity requiring special permission. Justice Bharatha Chakravarthy made the observation on Wednesday while confirming an order dated Sept 4, passed by the Bureau of Immigration cancelling the OCI permit granted to John Daniel.

Article Title: Imran Khan says grounds cited in FRRO notice ‘nebulous, contradictory’, seeks details
Article Text:
Khan said that he has not been supplied with the report submitted by Mumbai police or any related material, based on which the show-cause notice was issued.





MUMBAI: Actor Imran Khan has written to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) saying the grounds it has cited in its show-cause notice seeking to cancel his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status are nebulous and contradictory.The FRRO on Oct 17 had issued Khan, a US national, a show-cause after he allegedly participated in an anti-CEC stir organised by Tushar Gandhi of Hum Bharat Ke Log on Oct 10 at August Kranti Maidan.An earlier notice issued on Oct 14 asking him to leave India has been challenged in the Bombay high court and has been posted for hearing on Nov 2.Khan, in his reply of Oct 22, said a Mumbai police report cited by the FRRO was incomplete and sought details with evidence to enable him to send an effective response to the notice.He said the grounds in the show-cause notice (SCN) are nebulous and contradictory and sought disclosure of all the material the FRRO is relying on to ensure transparency, fairness and accountability in the decision-making process as required by the Citizenship Act.The principles of natural justice need compliance, Supreme Court says, and an OCI cardholder needs to be informed of details before resorting to a proposed stripping of such status, he contended.Khan said that he has not been supplied with the report submitted by Mumbai police or any related material, based on which the show-cause notice was issued.He asked for disclosure of the material on record on the basis of which the FRRO appears to have formed a provisional view that his OCI is liable to be cancelled.He said the material be presented to him swiftly since the Oct 17 notice gave him only 15 days, or till Nov 1, to respond.The FRRO appears to have formed a provisional opinion that his OCI is liable to be cancelled, said Khan, and cited Supreme Court judgments.He said he ought to be given all evidence relied on by the police and be allowed to examine it to be able to effectively respond to the SCN and provisional view the FRRO has taken.The actor said a quoted statement attributed to him in the SCN, “which has also been relied upon by the Mumbai police in its report, is incomplete.”“Mumbai police have not even attempted to record my statement in connection with the registration of FIR,” he added. The police lodged a first information report (FIR) for unlawful assembly against several persons including Khan, alleging his presence along with protestors.On Oct 14, the FRRO first issued the actor, who holds a US passport, a ‘Leave India notice’ invoking Immigration and Foreigners Act of 2025, for allegedly flouting its provisions.On Oct 27, the Bombay high court kept the leave India notice in abeyance after Centre sought a short adjournment to Nov 2 to enable Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to appear in the matter.
Article Summary: Imran Khan has written to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) He said the grounds it has cited in its show-cause notice seeking to cancel his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status are nebulous and contradictory.
