Article Title: Where did they vanish? Bengaluru loses 44 lakh voters, govt to trace them
Article Text:
Bengaluru has reported a significant decrease in its electorate after the final electoral roll was published recently.





BENGALURU: Where did they go? That is the question the state govt wants answered after Bengaluru’s electorate shrank by nearly 44 lakh, from 1.03 crore to 59.1 lakh, in the final roll published on Oct 27 after the special intensive revision (SIR). The 43.1% fall is part of a net deletion of 75 lakh voters across Karnataka A section of ministers told TOI the govt is likely to come up at Thursday’s cabinet meeting. Congress is using technology to check whether deleted names have been added to other booths or removed from the rolls altogether. “A few lakh may have kept their votes elsewhere, but a straight 50% drop is quite unheard of,” they added.The govt will not rush into accepting or rejecting the roll. “If 65 lakh people have permanently shifted out of their polling stations or constituencies, where have they been added?” one minister asked.They pointed out that ECI stopped accepting Form 6 during the two month exercise, which may have left many unable to enrol at new locations. “Since Karnataka has time until the next general elections, we will identify those who may have been disenfranchised or shifted but could not enrol at their new booths,” they said.One minister called the SIR exclusionary. “We will have to study the final roll and take a judicious decision on those removed,” he added.Home and IT-BT minister Priyank Kharge said the process was designed to favour the BJP. “The SIR is a flawed process, and we will review the final list. In Chittapura alone, Form 7 was distributed for 40 people, and this has been established. A complaint has been registered. Prima facie, a few communities are being targeted,” he said.The Greater Bengaluru Authority’s final roll has 28.7 lakh men, 30.4 lakh women and 674 voters in the other category. Nearly 47 lakh names were listed under the absent, shifted, dead, duplicate and others (ASDDO) category across 28 constituencies. Of these, 32.7 lakh were marked permanently shifted, over 7 lakh absent, over 3 lakh dead and 63,549 duplicates.Bengaluru South saw the most deletions at over 3.6 lakh, followed by Mahadevapura (nearly 3 lakh), Bommanahalli (over 2.6 lakh) and KR Puram (over 2.5 lakh). All four are held by BJP MLAs. Shivajinagar, with a sizeable minority population, lost 81,236 names. Last year, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had alleged large-scale inclusion of fake voters in Mahadevapura ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.Chief electoral officer V Anbukkumar said Tuesday that no eligible voter was deleted merely because Form 7 applications were submitted in bulk, and that eligible Form 6 applicants were included after verification. “There should be no apprehension that eligible voters have been left out arbitrarily. The process has been transparent and lawful,” he said.He said fewer than 1,000 foreigners had been detected, most of them reportedly from Nepal. The rolls will continue to be updated after publication of the final list, he added.BoxGovt should not accept SIR final electoral roll, says civil societyThe anti-SIR coalition in Karnataka Wednesday urged the state govt to not accept the final electoral roll prepared through the special integrated revision (SIR) process in the state. Noor Sridhar, a leader of the Coalition, demanded that a social audit, public hearing, and public scrutiny be conducted regarding this process. Addressing the media, the coalition pointed at the flaws in the SIR process—including allegations that the names of eligible voters have been dropped from the list—and the resulting impact on the right to vote be taken seriously. Indhudhar Honnapura, a DSS activist and noted writer, said the ECI made a mountain of haystack and lashed out at the massive expenditure to carry out an unscientific process which excludes people and has not seen many illegal migrants identified.
Article Summary: Bengaluru's electorate shrank by nearly 44 lakh, from 1.03 crore to 59.1 lakh. The 43.1% fall is part of a net deletion of 75 lakh voters across Karnataka. Congress is using technology to check whether deleted names have been added to other booths or removed from the rolls altogether.

Article Title: From hydrogen buses to nuclear power, green energy to drive Odisha’s next industrial wave: Vishal Dev
Article Text:
Vishal Kumar Dev

Odisha

targets 10.96 GW of renewable capacity by 2030. What are the key hurdles and emerging technologies being explored?

What improvements can consumers expect in reliability, service and tariffs?

How critical is reliable and affordable power to Odisha’s industrial push?

Will coal remain Odisha’s energy backbone over the next decade?

What role do you see for nuclear power in Odisha?

How is Odisha making its power infrastructure cyclone-resilient?

What would define a successful transformation of Odisha’s power sector by 2030?





The target includes 7,500 MW solar, 2,000 MW wind, 1,200 MW pumped storage and 260 MW small hydro. We have already approved renewable projects of more than 11,500 MW through the state’s single window clearance committee.The biggest hurdle is availability of contiguous land for utility-scale solar. We are, therefore, focusing on floating solar and Agri-PV. Odisha has awarded 1,000 MW floating solar capacity at Rengali reservoir, while a tender for 225 MW floating solar plus battery storage at Upper Indravati will be floated soon. We have also awarded a 125 MW/500 MWh standalone battery storage project.For wind energy, our immediate focus is onshore potential. Three wind-resource assessment masts have been installed and initial observations are encouraging. Offshore wind can be progressively evaluated as technology and infrastructure mature.We are also exploring geothermal and nuclear power, green hydrogen mobility and surface hydrokinetic turbines. Five hydrogen-powered buses are being introduced.Odisha met peak demand of 6,242 MW this year without a single minute of scheduled load shedding, while transmission availability has remained above 99.97% since 2020-21.Expansion of SCADA, distribution and feeder automation will help detect and resolve faults faster. Faster rollout of prepaid smart meters will improve billing transparency and give consumers greater control over consumption.Reliable, quality power is fundamental to industrial growth. Steel, aluminium and chemicals, besides emerging sectors such as green hydrogen and green ammonia, need uninterrupted and increasingly clean, competitively priced electricity.We are preparing to facilitate round-the-clock renewable power for upcoming green hydrogen and ammonia projects at Paradip and Gopalpur. Odisha is targeting around 4.5 MMTPA green ammonia production by 2030.Odisha’s transition will be progressive, not abrupt. Coal will continue providing stability and energy security in the medium term, but its role will steadily reduce as renewable energy backed by storage expands. Thermal power’s share is expected to decline from around 48% in FY 2030 to 39% in FY 2036 and about 26% by FY 2047.We will need not only more renewable energy, but also firm, low-carbon power that can be available round-the-clock. And nuclear energy has the potential to play an important role in that transition. Along with pumped storage and battery storage, nuclear can complement solar and wind and provide the reliability required for a diversified, low-carbon electricity system.The state intends to work closely with the Centre on site identification, feasibility assessment and appropriate partnership structures. Odisha has also provided in-principle approvals to NTPC and Adani Power to undertake site surveys and feasibility studies for potential nuclear power projects in the state. Ultimately, Odisha’s objective is clear — to combine renewable energy, storage and firm low-carbon generation to deliver clean, reliable and competitive power for our industries and our people.Successive cyclones since the 1999 Super Cyclone have shown that stronger assets, reliable early warnings and advance mobilisation are critical.OPTCL has planned infrastructure upgrades of around Rs 15,950 crore by 2030, including cyclone-resilient towers designed for basic wind speeds of 55 metres per second, selective underground cabling, modern substations and ring networks providing alternative supply paths. DISCOMs have planned Rs 6,750 crore capex over the next five years.Three achievements — delivering 10.96 GW of renewable energy addition across solar, wind, small hydro, pumped storage and battery storage; creating a resilient, future-ready grid capable of providing reliable electricity despite extreme weather; and using green power to drive Odisha’s next wave of industrialisation, particularly green hydrogen, green steel and low-carbon manufacturing.The real measure will be turning clean energy into reliable power for people and a long-term competitive advantage for Odisha’s industries.
Article Summary: Odisha met peak demand of 6,242 MW this year without a single minute of scheduled load shedding. Coal will continue providing stability and energy security in the medium term. Thermal power’s share is expected to decline from around 48% in 2030 to 39% in 2036 and about 26% by 2047.

Article Title: Bengaluru man pays Rs 12,500 monthly for 40 months in Rs 5 lakh chit scheme, gets only Rs 20,000; consumer commission orders company to pay Rs 4.07 lakh with interest
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only.





BENGALURU: Vishnuprasad paid Rs 12,500 every month for 40 months to complete a Rs 5 lakh chit fund scheme run by Samith Chits Pvt Ltd. But after he won the bid in May 2025, the company paid him only Rs 20,000, leaving Rs 4,07,940 unpaid.The consumer commission has now directed the company to pay the outstanding amount with 6.5% annual interest from the date the consumer complaint was filed until realisation. It has also ordered Samith Chits to pay Rs 3,000 towards proceedings costs, holding that the failure to pay the prize money amounted to deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice.President Syed Anser Khaleem and two members pronounced the order on September 28, 2026.According to the complaint, Vishnuprasad's chit scheme ended in June 2025. After he successfully bid for the chit in May, the company issued two cheques towards the amount due — one for Rs 1 lakh, dated July 5, 2025, and another for Rs 3,27,940, dated July 15, 2025.Vishnuprasad presented the first cheque on July 17 through his bank account in Ramamurthy Nagar. It was returned unpaid with the endorsement "Funds Insufficient".The second cheque, presented on July 24, was also dishonoured for insufficient funds.After receiving only Rs 20,000 despite follow-ups, Vishnuprasad issued a legal notice under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, which deals with cheque dishonour. He also initiated two cases before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate court in Bengaluru, numbered CC No. 72718/2025 and CC No. 72660/2025, before approaching the consumer commission.The commission examined Vishnuprasad's affidavit and supporting documents, including the company's brochure, its statement, copies of the cheques and records confirming their dishonour.Samith Chits did not appear despite being served notice and was placed ex parte on July 24, 2026. With the complaint and supporting evidence undisputed in the consumer proceedings, the commission held the company liable for failing to pay the outstanding chit amount.It also clarified that the cheque-dishonour cases did not prevent Vishnuprasad from seeking relief under consumer protection law. Citing Section 100 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the commission noted that remedies under the Act are in addition to those available under other laws.Samith Chits has been directed to comply within 30 months of receiving the order and submit a compliance report to the commission within 45 days of receipt.
Article Summary: Vishnuprasad paid Rs 12,500 every month for 40 months to complete a Rs 5 lakh chit fund scheme run by Samith Chits Pvt Ltd. But after he won the bid in May 2025, the company paid him only Rs 20,000. The consumer commission has now directed the company to pay the outstanding amount with 6.5% annual interest.

Article Title: Mumbai man books Panvel flat for Rs 50 lakh in 2015, waits nearly 10 years for possession; consumer commission orders developer to refund Rs 86 lakh with 9% interest
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





MUMBAI: Observing that a flat purchaser “cannot be expected to wait indefinitely” for possession and that the developer’s failure to hand over possession by the agreed deadline amounted to deficiency in service, a district consumer commission has directed M/s Soundlines Eco Homes and its partners to jointly and severally refund Rs 86.37 lakh (inclusive of interest) to a homebuyer over delayed possession in the “Sound Delight” project at Panvel. The commission allowed the complaint filed by Mulund resident Tapan Visaria. The pay out included the paid amount of Rs 45 lakh alongwith nine percent annual interest calculated from Dec 31, 2016, the contractual date of possession, until actual realization. He will also receive Rs 75,000 towards costs of litigation and mental agony.The commission refused to separately award Rs 5.23 lakh towards interest paid on the housing loan, relying on the Supreme Court’s decision. It was observed that the complainant had independently availed of a loan from the State Bank of India and was contractually liable to repay the loan with applicable interest. “The mere fact that the complainant incurred interest expenditure to arrange funds for purchasing the flat does not, by itself, make the opposite parties liable to reimburse that expenditure,” the Commission said while rejecting that head of claim.Visaria had booked the flat measuring 876 sq ft. carpet area, on the third floor of D-Wing in the project at Village Aashte, Taluka Panvel, District Raigad, for a total consideration of Rs 50.52 lakh. The agreement for sale was executed on Aug 7, 2015 and subsequently registered. According to the complainant, the developer had promised possession on or before Dec 31, 2016, but repeatedly extended the timeline, with the MahaRERA website later reflecting an extension up to Sept 30, 2026.The complainant alleged that he paid around Rs 45.45 lakh towards the flat consideration, apart from Rs 1.38 lakh towards VAT, GST and other taxes, Rs 2.53 lakh towards stamp duty and Rs 30,000 towards registration charges. He also claimed that amenities advertised in the project brochure, including an entrance gate with waterfall, clubhouse, rooftop shamiyana, amphitheatre and children’s play area, were either cancelled or not provided as promised.The opposite parties, including the partnership firm and its partners did not appear despite service of notices. The matter was therefore proceeded ex parte by order dated April 16, 2024. Taking note of the unrebutted material placed by the complainant, the commission said the agreement, bank statements, demand letters, email correspondence, photographs and loan interest certificate established that the flat had been booked and substantial payment had been made. “The evidence on record establishes that the opposite parties failed to deliver possession within the agreed period and have not furnished any satisfactory explanation for the delay. Such failure amounts to deficiency in service,” the commission held.
Article Summary: A district consumer commission has directed M/s Soundlines Eco Homes and its partners to jointly and severally refund Rs 86.37 lakh. The commission allowed the complaint filed by Mulund resident Tapan Visaria. The pay out included the paid amount of Rs 45 lakh alongwith nine percent annual interest calculated from Dec 31, 2016, the contractual date of possession.

Article Title: Chennai-bound flights are 23.9% cheaper when booked a month ahead than a day before departure, while Ahmedabad flyers face a 60.6% fare gap and Bengaluru sees just 5%
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only.

Median fare-time index by days before departure, 7 routes into Chennai against all routes. Captured on 28 October 2026.

What does the fare-time index mean?

Which route punishes late booking most?

How the seven routes compare

Route Flights per day (approx) Ahmedabad to Chennai 3 Pune to Chennai 2 Kolkata to Chennai 7 Hyderabad to Chennai 9 Mumbai to Chennai 12 Delhi to Chennai 13 Bengaluru to Chennai 14

What should a traveller consider?

About this data

TOI-DPA Airline Price Index is a joint initiative of The Times of India and Decimal Point Analytics.

Source: Decimal Point Analytics Airline Price Index





Across seven routes into Chennai, booking a flight 30 days before departure cost 23.9 per cent less than booking the day before, according to fares captured on the morning of 28 October 2026. That compares with a saving of 13.7 per cent across the broader network, making Chennai 10.2 percentage points better than the national figure. All seven routes into the city were cheaper at 30 days than at the day-before mark.The chart shows the fare-time index by booking horizon for Chennai routes against the network.The TOI-DPA Airline Price Index sets each route's day-before fare at 100 and expresses every other booking time as a number against it. A reading below 100 means fares at that booking horizon were lower than the day-before fare on the same route. A reading above 100 means they were higher. The index is built over a longer window than a single morning, so it reflects a pattern across multiple departure dates, not just one snapshot.For Chennai, the index stood at 78.7 at 90 days before departure, fell to 74.8 at 60 days, edged up to 76.1 at 30 days, climbed to 87.0 at 7 days, and reached 100.0 the day before.For the network, the corresponding readings were 88.1, 85.8, 86.3, 90.5, and 100.0. The lowest point on the Chennai curve was at 60 days, making that the cheapest booking horizon across the seven routes.The route where waiting hurts most is Ahmedabad to Chennai. Its index at 30 days was 62.3, meaning someone who booked the day before paid 60.6 per cent more than someone who booked 30 days out. Ahmedabad to Chennai has approximately 3 flights per day into Chennai, making it a thinner route than most others in this group.At the other end, Bengaluru to Chennai showed the smallest penalty for late booking. Its 30-day index was 95.3, and the extra cost for booking the day before was 5.0 per cent. With approximately 14 flights per day, it is the most frequent route among the seven, and the fare gap between booking horizons is narrow by comparison.Flight counts move between captures, so these figures should be read as approximate.The index points to 60 days before departure as the lowest-cost booking horizon across the seven Chennai routes, with the 30-day mark also well below the day-before fare. On the Ahmedabad to Chennai route, the difference between booking 30 days ahead and booking the day before was 60.6 per cent, a gap large enough to be worth planning around. On Bengaluru to Chennai, the same gap was only 5.0 per cent, so the timing of a booking matters far less on that corridor. These are patterns in advertised fares, not guarantees; any single quote can move.These are advertised fares and medians across routes, not what any passenger finally paid, and a quote visible on one morning can move. All fares were captured on the morning of 28 October 2026. The data does not record which airline charged a fare, so it cannot say who sets these prices. Fare data was not available in this capture for Mumbai to Pune and Pune to Mumbai. The percentages come from the tracker's fare-time index, which is built over a longer window than a single morning. This compares what different departure dates cost when quoted at different booking times, not what one flight cost as its date approached. Flight counts move between captures, so how busy a route is should be read as approximate.The Chennai booking curve sits consistently below the national network curve at every horizon from 90 days to 7 days before departure, and the 10.2-percentage-point advantage at the 30-day mark is driven in large part by routes with fewer daily flights, where the spread between early and late fares is widest. On the busiest corridors into the city, that spread narrows sharply, so the benefit of early booking is not uniform across all seven routes.
Article Summary: The TOI-DPA Airline Price Index sets each route's day-before fare at 100 and expresses every other booking time as a number against it. The index is built over a longer window than a single morning, so it reflects a pattern across multiple departure dates, not just one snapshot. The lowest point on the Chennai curve was at 60 days, making that the cheapest booking horizon across the seven routes.

Article Title: Jaipur man finds just 4g chips in Lay’s packet marked 15g; consumer commission orders PepsiCo to pay Rs 5,000 for mental harassment and Rs 3,000 for litigation costs within one month
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





JAIPUR: A consumer commission in Jaipur has held PepsiCo India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. liable after a complaint that a packet of Lay’s potato chips contained only 4 grams of chips against the declared net weight of 15 grams.According to a report by Live Law, the commission directed PepsiCo to refund Rs 5, with interest at 6% per annum from April 6, 2022, until payment. It also ordered the company to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs within one month of the order.If the company fails to pay the Rs 8,000 in compensation and litigation costs within the stipulated period, the amount will attract interest at 6% per annum from the date of the order until payment.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-II, Jaipur, comprising President Ashok Sharma and members Ajay Kumar and Supriya Agarwal, dismissed the complaint against retailer Metro Cash & Carry India Pvt. Ltd.The complaint was filed by Chandraman Jalan, proprietor of M/s Jalan Building and Hardware Store, who said he purchased various food items from Metro Cash & Carry on November 10, 2020, to serve guests at his residence, according to Live Law.The purchase included a packet of Lay’s potato chips manufactured by PepsiCo, for which an invoice was issued on the same day.According to Jalan, he noticed that the packet felt unusually light while serving the chips to his guests. He alleged that weighing its contents showed that it contained only 4 grams of chips, against the declared net weight of 15 grams.Jalan said he approached Metro Cash & Carry over the alleged shortage but was dissatisfied with the response. He subsequently filed a consumer complaint on April 6, 2022, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practices.Metro Cash & Carry contested the complaint, arguing that any shortage in the quantity of chips could have occurred during manufacturing and that the manufacturer should be held responsible.PepsiCo did not appear despite being served notice, and the proceedings against the company continued ex parte.After considering the complainant’s evidence, including the purchase invoice, the commission dismissed the complaint against Metro Cash & Carry and allowed it against PepsiCo.
Article Summary: A consumer commission in Jaipur has held PepsiCo India Holdings Pvt. Ltd. liable after a complaint that a packet of Lay’s potato chips contained only 4 grams of chips against the declared net weight of 15 grams. The commission directed PepsiCo to refund Rs 5, with interest at 6% per annum from April 6, 2022, until payment.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says AI is making the risk of job losses more real; warns of painful economic transition
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says AI is making the risk of job losses more real; warns of painful economic transition

Why AI may not eliminate 90% of jobs

Zoho founder urges workers to prepare for AI's impact

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could significantly change the job market, saying one skilled person using AI could perform work that previously required 10 people. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Sridhar Vembu said the risk was becoming increasingly real for people whose jobs involve working on computers, although he clarified that this does not mean 90% of such workers will become unemployed. “Any job performed on the computer has this risk now: one smart person using AI can perform the work of 10 people. The risk is getting ever more real,” Vembu wrote.In the post, he further stated that the growing capabilities of AI could lead to a major shift in how work is distributed across the economy. According to him, while some companies may need fewer employees to perform existing tasks, others could begin hiring for work they previously could not afford.However, Vembu clarified that higher productivity does not automatically mean that most workers will lose their jobs. He pointed out that the economic impact could be more complex, with changes in demand creating new opportunities alongside the risk of job losses.Explaining his view, Sridhar Vembu said industries that previously could not afford to hire software engineers or digital marketers might now be able to do so because AI could make their work more affordable.For instance, a small business that could not justify the cost of hiring a dedicated software engineer might find it easier to invest in software development when AI-assisted work reduces the time and resources required.Similarly, businesses that previously lacked the budget for digital marketing services could begin hiring professionals to help them reach customers.“This does not mean 90% of people working on a computer will have no work at all,” he said adding “Industries that previously could not afford to hire software engineers or digital marketers could afford them now, for example”.Sridhar Vembu described the likely outcome as a rebalancing across the economy, warning that the adjustment could be difficult for people whose jobs and skills are affected.As businesses adopt AI, the demand for certain tasks could decline while other skills and services become more valuable. Workers may need to adapt to changing job requirements, while companies could restructure teams and reconsider their hiring needs.The transition could also create challenges for people who need to learn new skills or move into different roles to remain competitive. Concluding his post, Vembu said accepting that the change is coming and preparing for it is the only way forward.“What it does mean is a rebalancing across the economy and that is painful when we go through it. The only thing we can do is to accept that it is coming and be prepared for it,” he wrote.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could significantly change the job market. He said one skilled person using AI could perform work that previously required 10 people. However, he clarified that higher productivity does not automatically mean that most workers will lose their jobs.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang names three countries that are leading the world in technology and manufacturing; and tells why he did not include US on the list
Article Text:
Jensen Huang

Why China did not make it to Huang’s list

US restrictions pushed China’s progress

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has identified three nations currently leading the globe in manufacturing and technology while also explaining why the US did not make his list, during a recent discussion with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Addressing China's industrial strengths, Huang pointed out that Beijing holds a unique competitive edge because its modern economic transformation directly coincided with the rise of the digital era. According to Huang, the global powers in production and advanced technology has revolved around three specific countries: Germany, Japan and China.“For the last 50 years, because of the current Industrial Revolution, which is computing and digital technology, the United States has largely exported its heavy manufacturing, its building, and its craft to China. So now the world has three (leaders) again. It’s Germany, Japan and China,” Huang said.Huang highlighted that China’s advantage stems from critical timing. Since its industrial surge unfolded alongside the rise of computing, its manufacturing base developed with digital infrastructure integrated from the start, leaving the country heavily computerised.“The advantage that China has is that they came into their industrial revolution, if you will, their economic transformation happened during precisely the time of the computer industry.They are quite computerized. China is probably the only nation today that is deep in manufacturing and deep in computer science. And very comfortable in both,” he highlighted.Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, the Nvidia CEO said that export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by the US have pushed China to speed up its own domestic chip manufacturing and strive for technological self-reliance.Current US trade rules prohibit the export of advanced processors to China, including Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence (AI) GPUs. Reports have claimed that several Chinese entities have managed to access that computing power through third-party data centers based in Southeast Asia.“We’ve definitely accelerated China’s initiatives, its nationalization of semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, and all of the industrial support that has been put into that sector, and so there’s no question we’ve accelerated that,” Huang said.Huang, however, said that despite intensified competition and China’s accelerated domestic initiatives, American tech firms remain well-prepared to take on competitive pressure “from anybody.”
Article Summary: Jensen Huang identified three nations currently leading the globe in manufacturing and technology: Germany, Japan and China. Huang explained why the US did not make his list, during a recent discussion with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Huang highlighted that China’s advantage stems from critical timing.
